themes_detail.label: Illegal Fireworks Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints spiked dramatically to 9 THIS WEEK, a 3500% jump from the 8-week baseline average of 0.2 complaints per week, suggesting either a coordinated incident, holiday anticipation activity, or emerging enforcement gap in CD 211.
evidence: 9 illegal fireworks complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Timing suggests possible holiday-driven activity or neighborhood-specific pattern
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD about enforcement response and whether this is neighborhood-wide or concentrated in specific blocks
Talk to residents about when fireworks are occurring (evening hours, specific dates) and whether complaints are being acted on quickly

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 65 THIS WEEK, a 364% increase from the 8-week average of 14 weekly complaints, indicating either widespread pothole formation, pavement failures, or a weather-triggered cascade of infrastructure issues.
evidence: 65 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 14.0 weekly average (z-score: 9.16)
Correlates with 7 street sweeping complaints last week (up 1020% from 0.6 baseline), suggesting cleanup backlog
Likely triggered by recent weather events or seasonal spring deterioration
reporting_angles: Conduct a block-level survey of Morris Park/Pelham Parkway main thoroughfares to map where worst conditions are and whether repairs are pending
Check DOT repair request queue and average response times for this district vs. citywide standards

themes_detail.label: Street & Sidewalk Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 30 LAST WEEK, a 400% increase from the 6.0 weekly baseline, paired with simultaneous spikes in fireworks and street sweeping complaints, suggesting multipronged disruption in public space.
evidence: 30 street/sidewalk noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 6.0 weekly average (z-score: 6.93)
Temporal overlap with fireworks spike (9 complaints this week) and street sweeping complaints (7 last week)
Suggests concentrated period of nighttime disruption or construction activity
reporting_angles: Identify specific streets/intersections where noise complaints clustered—construction sites, bars, or event venues
Interview community members about what time of day/night disturbances occur and whether NYPD is responding to noise complaints

themes_detail.label: Dirty Conditions & Sanitation Lag
themes_detail.summary: Dirty condition complaints reached 41 LAST WEEK, up 242% from the 12.0 weekly baseline, correlating with street sweeping complaints (7, up 1020%), indicating a possible street cleaning service failure or accumulation cycle.
evidence: 41 dirty condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 12.0 weekly average (z-score: 4.8)
7 street sweeping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 baseline (1020% increase)
Pattern suggests sanitation pickup or street sweeping schedule disruption
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Sanitation to understand whether there were staffing issues, truck breakdowns, or route delays affecting CD 211 last week
Map dirty condition complaints geographically to identify whether issue is district-wide or concentrated in specific neighborhoods

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Failures (2 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal condition complaints hit 24 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 357% spike from the 5.2 weekly baseline, suggesting either weather damage, maintenance backlog, or emerging electrical system failures in the district.
evidence: 24 traffic signal condition complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 5.2 weekly average (z-score: 4.49)
Timing suggests weather-triggered or aging infrastructure failure
Recurring budget request for streetscape improvements may indicate systemic aging
reporting_angles: Check with DOT for a list of malfunctioning signals reported in CD 211 and average repair times
Interview traffic-heavy intersections (Morris Park Ave, Pelham Parkway) to see if outages are affecting pedestrian/vehicle safety
